sections.h2: Which Connecticut laws set the rules between landlords and tenants?
sections.html:
Most of them sit in Title 47a of the General Statutes, which the legislature splits into chapters by subject. A landlord who plans to sell a rental will touch several chapters, so it helps to know which one answers which question.

ChapterSubject
830Rights and responsibilities of landlord and tenant
831Security deposits
832Summary process (eviction)
833Entry and detainer
833aPublic enforcement of health and safety standards in rented dwellings

The Connecticut Judicial Branch law library keeps a landlord and tenant page that links to these chapters, to forms, and to research reports from the Office of Legislative Research. It is a starting point for research, as the page itself says, and not legal advice.

sections.h2: What must a Connecticut landlord keep in working order?
sections.html:
Section 47a-7 requires a landlord to follow the building and housing codes that affect health and safety, and to keep the premises fit and habitable. The duty has exceptions where the tenant or a guest made the place unfit on purpose.

The list in the statute is practical.

  • Make repairs and do whatever is needed to keep the premises fit and habitable.
  • Keep the common areas clean and safe.
  • Maintain electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating and ventilating facilities, appliances and elevators that the landlord supplies or is required to supply, in good and safe working order.
  • Provide and maintain receptacles for ashes, garbage and other waste.

For a seller, these duties follow the house. A buyer who steps into the landlord's role takes on the same obligations, and an inspection that finds worn heating or plumbing in a rented unit can lower a buyer's offer. A buyer of an as-is investment property usually prices that risk in rather than asking for repairs.

sections.h2: When is rent late, and what can a landlord charge?
sections.html:
A tenant has a nine-day grace period after rent is due, and four days for a one-week tenancy. Only after that may a landlord terminate the rental agreement for nonpayment under sections 47a-23 to 47a-23b. The rule is in section 47a-15a.

If the lease has a valid written late-charge agreement, the landlord may charge a fee on a payment made after the grace period. The fee may not exceed the lesser of five dollars a day, up to a maximum of fifty dollars, or five percent of the late payment. Where a government or charitable entity pays part of the rent, the five percent applies to the tenant's share. A landlord may not charge more than one late fee on a single late payment, however long it stays unpaid.

When you sell, a buyer will ask for a rent roll and payment history. Accurate records of due dates, grace periods and any late fees save questions at closing.

sections.h2: Can a landlord show a rented home to buyers?
sections.html:
Yes, with limits. Section 47a-16 says a tenant may not unreasonably withhold consent for the landlord to enter to exhibit the dwelling unit to prospective or actual purchasers, along with entering to inspect or make repairs.

The same section keeps the tenant's privacy intact. A landlord may enter without consent in an emergency, as section 47a-16a permits, under a court order, or if the tenant has abandoned the premises. A landlord may not abuse the right of entry or use it to harass a tenant, and may enter only at reasonable times except in an emergency.

Showings in a rental are easier when the owner plans them with the tenant. Offering set windows, and keeping a short list of who is visiting, usually works better than repeated requests. A cash buyer who wants to view a tenant-occupied house can do a single visit instead of a series of open houses.

sections.h2: What happens to the tenant's security deposit when the landlord sells?
sections.html:
The deposit passes to the new owner. Under section 47a-21, any voluntary or involuntary transfer of a landlord's interest in residential real property to a successor is an assignment to that successor of the landlord's security interest in all deposits paid by the tenants.

The seller also has a duty to move the money. When real estate is transferred from a landlord, other than a receiver, to a successor, the landlord must withdraw the full amount of the deposits, with accrued interest, from the escrow account and deliver it to the successor. If the account holds deposits for other properties and has less than the total owed, the seller delivers a pro rata share for the property being sold.

The word successor in the chapter includes a person who gets the landlord's interest by purchase, foreclosure or otherwise. That is why the chapter treats a buyer as a landlord for deposit purposes.

  • Return deadline: not later than twenty-one days after the tenancy ends, or fifteen days after the tenant gives a written forwarding address, whichever is later.
  • What is returned: the full deposit plus accrued interest, less any damage deductions the landlord is allowed to take.

sections.h2: What must a new owner tell the tenants after closing?
sections.html:
Section 47a-6 puts a duty on the landlord, or a successor landlord, to tell the tenant in writing, at the time of succession, the name and address of the person authorized to manage the premises. The statute names a second person as well, so read the full text.

The Department of Housing posts mandatory landlord and tenant forms and notice forms on its website, and the Judicial Branch page links them. A buyer who takes over a rental should have the notice ready for closing day, along with the lease copies, the deposit transfer and any records on repairs or complaints.

Tenants do better when the owner tells them about a sale directly. A short written note that names the seller, the buyer and the new contact reduces confusion and missed rent.

sections.h2: Which tenants have extra protection from eviction?
sections.html:
Section 47a-23c limits evictions of older and disabled tenants in larger properties. It applies in a building or complex of five or more dwelling units, or in a mobile manufactured home park, to a tenant who is 62 or older or has a qualifying disability, along with some tenants who live with a relative who meets those conditions.

For those tenants a landlord may sue only on the grounds the statute lists, and a rent increase must be fair and equitable under the criteria in section 7-148c. A protected tenant who is aggrieved by a proposed increase may file with the fair rent commission in the town, if there is one, or go to Superior Court if there is none. The Judicial Branch page also lists Public Act 22-30, an act concerning fair rent commissions effective October 1, 2022.

A sale of the building is not one of the grounds. Buyers of small apartment buildings should ask for the age and status of each tenant before they agree on a price.

sections.h2: What should a Connecticut landlord do before selling a rental?
sections.html:
Gather the paper trail first. A short list will keep the sale on schedule.

  1. Copy each lease and any rental agreement, with rent amounts and dates.
  2. Confirm where each security deposit is held and how much interest has accrued.
  3. Write down repair requests and what was done under section 47a-7.
  4. Check whether any tenant falls under section 47a-23c.
  5. Decide whether to sell with tenants in place or after they leave, and put any move-out agreement in writing.

Selling to a cash investor is common for landlords with tired rentals. The buyer takes the property as-is and handles the leases after closing, so the owner does not need to make repairs, hold showings or wait for a mortgage approval.

faqs.q: What is the maximum security deposit in Connecticut?
faqs.a: The cap is two months' rent for a tenant under 62 and one month's rent for a tenant 62 or older under section 47a-21.

faqs.q: How soon must a landlord return a deposit?
faqs.a: A landlord must deliver the deposit with accrued interest, less allowed deductions, not later than 21 days after the tenancy ends or 15 days after a written forwarding address, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Does a new owner have to honor the existing lease?
faqs.a: The chapter treats a successor as a landlord and passes the deposits to the successor. Whether a lease continues depends on its terms and on the notice and court rules, so read the lease and ask an attorney.

faqs.q: Can a landlord enter a rental without notice?
faqs.a: Only in an emergency, under a court order, as permitted by section 47a-16a, or when the unit has been abandoned. Otherwise entry needs the tenant's consent and a reasonable time.

faqs.q: Where can I find Connecticut landlord and tenant forms?
faqs.a: The Judicial Branch law library page for landlord and tenant law links housing forms, and the Department of Housing posts mandatory notice forms and a model lease.
